project.name: Coudray NSCLC Mutation Landmark
project.summary: Coudray NSCLC Mutation Landmark is a standalone literature project created from the reference layer of the supplied gene-mutation paper so that the MemoryTonic collection can contain multiple comparable projects instead of only one synthesized overview. The practical purpose of this project is to create graph structure that supports bridges, cross-paper comparison, and clearer separation between evidence types. In the original uploaded collection there was only a single project, which meant there could be no bridge entities by definition even if the research itself was thoughtful. This project addresses that structural limitation by representing one coherent slice of the cited literature as its own graph-ready unit. The focus here is: A project built from the anchor paper's description of the 2018 Coudray study that established early proof that non-small cell lung cancer histopathology could support mutation prediction for driver genes such as EGFR and KRAS. The project therefore captures the entities, methods, validation themes, and clinically relevant concepts that recur in this part of the literature, especially histopathology images, mutation prediction, precision oncology, and the conditions under which claims should be trusted. It also encodes the difference between promising internal results and stronger external evidence. By storing this literature slice as a separate project in the same Gene Mutation Research collection, the graph can now discover which concepts are repeated across projects and which themes are unique to a single paper or subfield. That is what makes bridge entities meaningful in this platform: not a single long paper, but several connected projects that share important vocabulary, methods, datasets, and limitations.
narrative_flow: This project isolates one coherent slice of the cited gene-mutation literature so that it can function as its own graph unit inside the collection.
It focuses on recurring entities such as histopathology, mutation status, validation design, and clinically meaningful molecular targets.
The project converts those themes into structured relationships so the collection can compare methods, datasets, and claims across separate projects.
Its main value inside MemoryTonic is to create shared vocabulary with neighboring projects, enabling bridge entities and cross-paper reasoning.
Together with the other uploaded literature projects, it turns the gene-mutation collection from a single summary into a true multi-project research graph.

relationships.description: Histopathology images provide the visual substrate from which mutation-linked morphology is inferred, making tissue appearance the key non-genomic evidence source for computational mutation prediction pipelines across this literature project.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper repeatedly frames pathology morphology as the observable phenotype of latent genomic events.

relationships.description: Somatic mutation status guides targeted therapy selection and molecular stratification in precision oncology, giving direct clinical relevance to any method that can estimate mutation state from pathology evidence.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper describes mutation profiling as foundational to personalized cancer therapy.

relationships.description: If pathology images can support mutation inference, they become useful to precision oncology screening because they are already produced in routine care and may prioritize who most needs confirmatory sequencing.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper frames image-based prediction as a triage and acceleration mechanism rather than only a research exercise.

relationships.description: Strong patient-level generalization is required before promising research metrics can be treated as clinically meaningful support for precision oncology workflows beyond the originating cohort.
relationships.evidence: The broader literature repeatedly distinguishes internal performance from stronger translational evidence.

relationships.description: External validation is the main empirical mechanism for establishing whether mutation-prediction systems generalize to unseen cohorts and institutions rather than only to familiar development data.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper and its cited literature emphasize external robustness as a key standard.

relationships.description: Interpretability supports clinical trust because researchers and clinicians need to know whether a mutation prediction rests on plausible morphology or unstable artefacts before it influences precision oncology decisions.
relationships.evidence: The cited reviews identify interpretability as a major open challenge for medical AI.

relationships.description: Variation in staining, tissue composition, cohort makeup, and acquisition conditions makes patient-level generalization a central challenge for histopathology-based mutation prediction even when proof-of-concept signal exists.
relationships.evidence: The literature repeatedly returns to robustness and external validation as unresolved needs.

relationships.description: Because pathology datasets vary across institutions and cohorts, claims made from histopathology-based mutation systems require external validation to demonstrate reproducibility and real robustness.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper highlights external validation as the stronger test across the field.

relationships.description: Histopathology-based mutation prediction literature repeatedly treats EGFR as an important actionable target, helping connect image evidence to directly relevant lung-cancer molecular decisions.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper explicitly highlights EGFR as a clinically actionable example.

relationships.description: Histopathology-based mutation prediction literature also repeatedly targets KRAS, making it a natural bridge entity across lung-cancer and multimodal mutation studies.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper names KRAS as a recurring and clinically relevant driver mutation.

relationships.description: Image-level training can increase learnable signal and improve internal performance without automatically guaranteeing patient-level generalization, because tile-level success and new-patient robustness are not the same claim.
relationships.evidence: The anchor paper itself separates improved patch-level learning from true generalization.

relationships.description: The TCGA LUAD and LUSC cohort provides paired lung-cancer histopathology data that ground and connect multiple projects in this collection, especially in early and benchmark-oriented mutation studies.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper repeatedly uses TCGA as a foundational resource.

relationships.description: EGFR remains a clinically actionable mutation target whose status directly influences targeted therapy reasoning, making it a recurring bridge between molecular pathology studies and real treatment logic.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper uses EGFR as a central example of actionable mutation relevance.

relationships.description: KRAS mutation status strongly shapes treatment framing and biological interpretation in oncology, so it repeatedly appears as a meaningful target in pathology-based mutation prediction work.
relationships.evidence: The supplied paper explicitly highlights KRAS in its clinical framing.
